title: Language models can explain neurons in language models
one_liner: 让 GPT-4 给神经元写解释，再根据解释预测新文本上的激活，用预测与真实激活的相关性检查解释质量。
classification_reason: 用文字压缩并预测 MLP 神经元激活，再与真实激活及消融评分比较；主要解释输入与激活的相关模式，并非恢复完整的因果计算机制。

related.reason: 两者都用自然语言描述内部激活，但本工作主要用解释模拟神经元反应，NLA 将解释用于激活压缩与重构。

problem.text: 模型里有大量神经元，研究者难以逐个查看它们对什么文本响应。作者研究能否让语言模型批量生成可读解释，并给解释一个可比较的分数，帮助筛选值得继续研究的内部行为。

gap.text: 看几个高激活样本，容易给出似乎合理却过于宽泛的解释。单词查表又可能预测得很好，却没有概括复杂的上下文规律。这项工作将生成解释与检验解释分开，避免只凭解释读起来是否顺畅来判断。

method.text: 解释器看到五段高激活文本及归一化到 0—10 的 token 激活，写出自然语言假设。模拟器只根据假设和新文本预测激活，再与真实激活计算相关系数。生成与评分使用不同文档；评分可选随机文本，或高激活与随机文本各五段。作者还比较消融评分、人工偏好和单词基线，并用模型生成的反例修改解释。

trace.text: 一个神经元实际响应“not all”，但初始解释只说它识别“all”。作者让 GPT-4 生成符合原解释的新句子，发现普通“all”并不总能激活神经元，再把这些反例交给解释器修改。这能纠正过宽解释，不过修订后的解释有时又会过窄。

inputs_outputs.text: 输入需要目标模型的内部访问权限、文本样本与逐 token 激活，并需要解释器和模拟器。输出包括神经元的文字解释、模拟激活、评分和可视化数据。主要研究对象是 GPT-2 的 MLP 神经元，GPT-4 通常同时担任解释器和模拟器；还进行了模型大小、训练时间与激活函数对照。

results.text: 默认方法在 GPT-2 神经元上，高激活加随机样本的平均相关得分为 0.151，纯随机样本为 0.037。307,200 个神经元中，5,203 个在前一设置得分超过 0.7，纯随机设置则为 732 个。人工构造的 19 个解释谜题中，基线解出 5 个，加入修订后再解出 4 个；这些数量不能解释为已经完整理解模型相同比例的计算。

contributions.text: 作者提供了“解释—模拟—评分”的可扩展流程，并公开 GPT-2 XL 神经元解释与工具。更重要的是，解释被当作可预测新证据的假设，而不是自动生成的标签；对反例、评分偏差和解释对象的实验，也说明了下一步应改进哪里。

limitations.text: 多数神经元仍解释得不好，单个神经元还可能混合多个特征。相关得分高不代表准确恢复其下游作用：相关 0.9 的解释，平均消融得分仍只有随机设置约 0.3、混合设置约 0.6。解释器与模拟器可能共享偏差，随机评分也容易受稀疏激活和样本量影响。作者明确说主要解释相关性，而非机制。

cost.text: 流程要先收集大量激活，再为神经元调用解释器和模拟器，计算开销较高。复现原版 GPT-4 模拟还依赖 token 概率；论文脚注指出，当时公开的 GPT-4 聊天 API 没有提供所需 logprobs。上下文长度和不同模型的分词方式也会影响复现，不能只凭有一个聊天接口就假定可原样运行。

relevance.text: 知识库分析：这是自动可解释性研究的桥接工具，可与 SAE 特征和自然语言激活解码比较。修订的是解释和可解释方向，并非让目标模型递归改进自身；论文没有验证解释驱动的 RSI。

en.one_liner: Uses GPT-4 to explain neurons and predict their activations on new text, scoring explanations by correlation with real activations.

sections.problem: Understanding millions of neurons manually does not scale. The authors automate readable explanations and quantitative testing to help researchers select internal behaviors for further study.
sections.gap: Top-activation examples can encourage plausible but overly broad explanations. Token lookup tables may predict well without summarizing contextual patterns. The method separates explanation generation from testing rather than relying on plausibility alone.
sections.method: An explainer sees five high-activation excerpts with token activations normalized to 0–10. A simulator predicts activations for different documents using only the explanation. Correlation with real activations supplies the score. Evaluation uses random excerpts or five high-activation plus five random excerpts. Ablation, human preferences, token baselines and counterexample-based revisions provide additional checks.
sections.trace: A neuron responds to “not all,” but its initial explanation centers on “all.” Generated sentences reveal that ordinary uses of “all” fail to activate it. Revising with this evidence can correct overbreadth, although revisions sometimes become too narrow.
sections.inputs_outputs: Inputs require internal model access, text and token-level activations, plus explainer and simulator models. Outputs include explanations, simulated activations, scores and visualization data. Main experiments use GPT-2 MLP neurons with GPT-4 assistants, alongside size, training-time and activation-function comparisons.
sections.results: Mean correlation scores are 0.151 on top-and-random excerpts and 0.037 on random-only excerpts. Of 307,200 neurons, 5,203 exceed 0.7 in the former setting and 732 in the latter. The baseline solves 5 of 19 constructed neuron puzzles; revision solves four more. These figures do not measure the proportion of model computation fully understood.
sections.contributions: The work provides a scalable explain–simulate–score workflow and releases GPT-2 XL explanations and tools. Explanations are testable hypotheses rather than labels, with experiments exposing bottlenecks in evidence, scoring and the choice of explanatory units.
sections.limitations: Most neurons remain poorly explained and may combine multiple features. High correlation does not recover downstream function: explanations with correlation 0.9 average roughly 0.3 random-only or 0.6 top-and-random ablation scores. Shared assistant biases, sparse activations and sampling noise further limit interpretation. The authors explicitly distinguish correlations from mechanisms.
sections.cost: Activation collection and repeated assistant calls are expensive. The original GPT-4 simulator also needs token probabilities; a footnote notes that its public chat API did not then expose the required logprobs. Context limits and tokenization differences are additional reproduction constraints.
sections.relevance: Library analysis: This is a bridge tool for automated interpretability, complementing SAE features and natural-language activation decoding. It revises explanations and directions, not the subject model’s own improvement mechanism, and does not demonstrate explanation-driven RSI.

related.natural-language-autoencoders: Both describe activations in natural language; this work simulates neuron responses, while NLA learns activation compression and reconstruction.
